messages:
maria: noticed an uptick in structured-json failures on eu-dedicated after yesterday's quant rollout (autocalib-v3). customer ticket RN-482 showed truncated arrays and null choices. tagging eng-runtime and infra.

jin: saw the same in telemetry — structured_json_fail_rate +5.1% around 2798762400. Pulled quick profiler. Kernel selection looks different on canary: mix-autosteer chose fp8_attn_v2 + int4_gemm_opt, with layer 18 falling back to fp32_attention. KV hit rate dropped.

jin: ```
kernel_selection_summary:
  policy: mix-autosteer-v2
  chosen_kernels: [fp8_attn_v2, int4_gemm_opt, int4_bias_fuse]
  fallback_layers: [18->fp32_attention]
  p50_latency_ms: 35 -> 41
  avg_batch_size: 2.9 -> 5.1
  kv_cache_hit: 0.93 -> 0.86
```

sam: can you paste one minimal repro input (sanitized) and expected vs observed output? we need to know if the problem is generation alignment or postprocessing.

maria: repro (sanitized):

maria: ```
input: {"prompt":"{instructions: return JSON with fields 'items' (array) and 'meta' (object)}","max_tokens":300}
expected: {"items":[{"id":"1","value":"x"}],"meta":{"count":1}}
observed: {"items":[null],"meta":{}}
```

leo: that pattern — arrays replaced by nulls or shorter arrays — looks like token misalignment from KV indexing issues under mixed precision. we saw something similar with 4-bit relu-scale drift where attention indices got misapplied across tokens.

jin: pulled per-layer diagnostics for the failing trace:

jin: ```
per_layer_stats for request 2798765420:
  layer_17: activation_scale_fp8=0.0032 activation_scale_int4=0.0028 scale_delta_post_calib=+11%
  layer_18: token_drop_rate: baseline 0.4% -> 3.9%
  layer_18: nan_count: 0 -> 1 per 500 requests
  kv_index_shifts_detected: 0 -> 2 in suffix windows
```

sam: important question — was autocalib corpus identical to previous runs? small changes in range estimation can push clip thresholds and change quantized kernel trace behavior.

maria: rollout used autocalib-v3 (PR infra#4120). main changes: per-batch dynamic range estimation and per-layer clip tweaks. also changed kernel handshake order to prefer int4_gemm_opt on certain dims.

leo: handshake/order change + new scales is a plausible interaction vector. kernel A may assume scale semantics that changed subtly so the KV offsets or accumulation rounding differs.

jin: quick AB test locally: pin quant-profile to v2 (old) and replay the same requests. structured pass-rate returns to baseline. Perf delta: token cost +1.1%, latency roughly flat.

oncall-bot: ops action suggested: schedule rollback of quant-profile to v2 on canary clusters in eu.

ops: queued rollback job rb-20260319-07. window in 20m.

sam: I'll run eval set "structured-json-e2e-v5" across profiles: fp32, quant-v2, quant-v3. Will produce token-level diffs and schema-violation counts. ETA ~30m.

jin: also enabling extra per-layer verbose telemetry for next 3 hours on affected hosts (activation histograms, kv index checksums, kernel selection trace).

leo: proposed mitigations:
  - short term: rollback canary to quant-v2 and pin prod until root cause identified
  - mid term: add schema-based post-generation verifier into calibration CI + closed-set structured prompts test
  - longer term: conservative kernel handshake — if per-layer activation shift > threshold OR any nan count spike, force fp32 for that layer for this request

maria: agreement on short term. action items:
  1) rollback canary -> prod if telemetry normalizes
  2) run structured evals across profiles and attach diffs to incident ticket
  3) add CI gate in calibration pipeline to run a small suite of JSON-schema prompts
  4) instrument kv-cache flush hook during quant-profile switches to reduce stale index risk

sam: starting eval run now. initial small sample shows quant-v3 has schema-violation rate 3.8% vs quant-v2 0.5% vs fp32 0.2% on structured-json-e2e-v5. dumping full diff to ticket RN-482 and linking here when done.

jin: created telemetry alert: structured_json_fail_rate > 2% for 10m -> page oncall.

maria: cool — ops please monitor rollback and keep the canary window tight. if rollback fixes it we will keep v2 pinned and open a postmortem on autocalib-v3.

leo: note: also check batching heuristics. average batch size increased on canary which could change per-batch dynamic range estimates (per-batch autocalib plausible cause). suggest replay with original batching distribution to isolate.

maria: good catch. jin — can you replay with original batching histogram?

jin: replaying now against dev cluster with pinned batching. preliminary looks like structured failures drop but still slightly higher than v2 baseline. suggests both batching + kernel handshake play roles.

maria: ok let's proceed with rollback for safety, collect full eval diffs, then deep-dive into kernel handshake + per-batch autocalib logic. schedule a dedicated triage tomorrow 1100 UTC with eng-runtime + eng-ml + infra.

oncall-bot: rollback job rb-20260319-07 started on eu-canary-01.

maria: thanks everyone. will update this thread when we have post-rollback telemetry. :thumbsup:
